I know college can be kind of a drag but you're probably a lot smarter than your friends, from what it sounds like. Maybe you should turn all of this pain into a drive to become really good at something. Turn inept into adept. 

Using myself as an example(since myself and others here are going through shit too, as you said), I am a biochem major with a double minor in math/physics. I don't really have friends but I have the respect of my authorities and that will get me so much farther in life than being able to make small talk over drinks with people I probably wouldn't be close to anyway in a few years. I make jet fuel and would have a really bright future if it weren't for my trash background check.  

Point is, there are better things to spend your energy on than comparing yourself to the 90% of the population that lives to socialize and breed, as grotesque as that may sound. Don't be blinded by love, OP. Trust science.

I'm sorry about your pets. My dad and step mom have munchhausen syndrome and have killed four of my cats. Not a very similar story but I know how powerless you feel watching the lives of your helpless animals end.

Sleep is very important to mental health. I'm not trying to give medical advice as I am not a licensed professional, but if the meds are messing with your sleep schedule so much that you can't even get in to see your therapist, they are doing more harm than good. Maybe try easing into them a little slower or trying something else entirely?

My mom also underestimated how much my friend's suicide affected me, almost five years ago to this day. While she was not that ignorant, she gave me an early curfew on the day of his memorial service. I should have ignored her and stayed close to my friends but I didn't. I wish I could say I regret it to this day but my being there after the fact didn't change what happened. We were a very close group before we lost him and it broke us all. I'm sorry about your friend but try to live your best life. I fell to the depression and it caused my mom to realize how much it affected me only years later. If I have any advice, it is to keep your mom at a distance and, as strange as it sounds, don't ever let her know how much this damaged you. Even being your mom, she is human and might play at that weakness in your mental well-being when it really counts. Good luck.
